assets.content:
Subject: For the handbook questions that keep landing in your DMs
Preview text: orqAgent is live — put an agent over the policy docs, install it in Slack, and point people at the channel.

Put an answer-bot in Slack over your own handbook

Hi there,

orqAgent is live. You can now stand up an agent over your own handbook documents and put it in Slack, where it answers the policy questions that keep coming back to you.

Those answers usually exist already, written up in Notion or somewhere like it. Finding one means guessing at keywords and document titles until something turns up — which is why the question comes to you instead.

If you have priced out wiring this yourself — Slack events, a store to search, a model API — the prototype is the quick part. What follows is a production system the whole company uses, and it has no owner.

Here that assembly is configuration. Upload PDFs, docs or plain text; the agent retrieves the most relevant context for every query, with no vector DB to manage. Slack is an OAuth install — the bot replies to mentions and channel messages.

Before you open it to the whole company, the usage is visible while it runs: token usage per model, P95 latency and daily spend trends, tracked automatically without extra configuration.

Point one agent at one set of policy documents, connect a single channel, and read the first runs.

Create your first agent →

- the orqAgent team

P.S. Your first agent takes under two minutes to create, and no card is required.

emails.single_idea: The Slack handbook bot you have been scoping is now a configuration job over the docs you already keep — the retrieval layer is part of the platform, not something you stand up.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: A no-code platform (orqAgent) that connects to Notion and Slack over OAuth to let you build a Slack bot that answers questions from your handbook, without you having to build the retrieval/vector-DB layer yourself.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The email's premise — 'same handbook questions come back in the channel, and the answers sit several searches deep' — matches the profile's documented problem context (dev.to quote about repeated questions, ippon.tech quote about buried answers). The profile establishes this person is 'building or considering building' exactly this kind of bot, and the email's core offer (Slack+Notion RAG bot) lines up with the GitLab work-item quote about wanting a responder with Handbook/Docs/Issue Tracker access. Where the email goes further than the profile supports: it assumes the reader's current blocker is specifically the 'integration project' of building retrieval/vector DB from scratch — the profile doesn't establish they've already started building or hit that specific wall, just that they're 'standing up' or 'considering' one. So the general problem is supported, but the specific narrative of 'you're mid-build and stuck on plumbing' is email-only, not profile-confirmed.
assumed_experiences: Reader has already scoped or attempted a DIY Slack+retrieval+model integration — email-only, not confirmed by profile
Reader is currently frustrated by repeated handbook questions in Slack — profile-supported (GitLab/ippon quotes)
Reader knows what a 'vector database' is and would see not needing one as a relief — email-only assumption about technical background
Reader has decision authority to 'decide whether it belongs in front of the whole company' — email-only
reader_verdicts.problem_now: The repeated-question problem is documented as a real, ongoing pain in the profile's sourced context, not a hypothetical. But there's no established urgency or deadline — it's a standing annoyance, not a fire, and the profile doesn't say they've already tried and failed to build something.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: Between them, the agent retrieves the most relevant context for every question automatically — there is no vector database to stand up or keep running.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: It's a low-code/no-code platform for something the sourced problem context explicitly flags as needing production-grade reliability, not low-code tooling — so even if it solves the demo, I don't know if it holds up once the whole company depends on it. Also no mention of what happens with sensitive HR/policy docs going through a third-party OAuth connection, and no pricing beyond '1,500 free credits' with no sense of what that buys.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: told me what happens to document access/permissions when Notion connects over OAuth — do all pages sync, can I scope it, and what does 1,500 credits actually get me before I hit a paywall
fixes: Standing up a Slack bot over your handbook reads like an integration project.

Subject: The same handbook question, back in the channel
Preview text: The answer sits several searches deep in Notion. An agent over those pages can take the question instead.

Answer handbook questions in Slack without building retrieval

Hi there,

Standing up a Slack bot over your handbook reads like an integration project.

Slack events on one side, a retrieval layer in the middle, a model API on the other — and something to keep working afterwards. Meanwhile the same handbook questions come back in the channel, and the answers sit several searches deep.

orqAgent is now available: a no-code platform for building AI agents. For this job, it is one agent and two connections.

Notion connects over OAuth and syncs your page and database content into the agent's knowledge base. Slack installs over OAuth, and the bot replies to mentions and channel messages.

Between them, the agent retrieves the most relevant context for every question automatically — there is no vector database to stand up or keep running.

Create one agent, connect the handbook, and ask it one real policy question in a Slack channel. Read what comes back, then decide whether it belongs in front of the whole company.

Create your first agent →

- the orqAgent team

P.S. No card required to start — new accounts get 1,500 free credits.
